subject: biology

items.q: Where is DNA found in a cell?
items.correct: Mainly in the nucleus, but also in mitochondria (and chloroplasts).
items.why: Most DNA is nuclear, but mitochondria (and plant chloroplasts) carry their own DNA.

items.q: Does each gene control one characteristic on its own?
items.correct: No — many traits are polygenic and affected by the environment.
items.misconception: Yes, every trait is controlled by a single gene alone.
items.why: Most characteristics involve several genes plus environment; genes are made of DNA.

items.q: Will a recessive allele die out over generations?
items.correct: No — it persists, carried by heterozygotes.
items.misconception: Yes, recessive alleles are weak and disappear.
items.random_wrong: Dominant alleles are always the most common.
items.why: 'Dominant/recessive' describes expression, not frequency; recessive alleles are hidden in carriers.
